text: Jesus got into a boat, crossed over, and came to his own town.
And some men brought him a paralyzed man lying on a bed. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, "Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven."
At that, some of the scribes said to themselves, "This man is blaspheming."
Knowing their thoughts, Jesus said, "Why do you harbor evil in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins"—then he said to the paralytic, "Get up, take your bed, and go home."
And the man got up and went home.
When the crowds saw it, they were filled with awe and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
As Jesus went on from there, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth, and he said to him, "Follow me." And Matthew got up and followed him.
Later, while Jesus was reclining at table in the house, many tax collectors and sinners came and were eating with him and his disciples.
When the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?"
Hearing them, he said, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.
Go and learn what this means: 'I desire mercy, not sacrifice.' For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners."
Then John's disciples came to him and asked, "Why is it that we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?"
Jesus answered, "Can the wedding guests mourn while the bridegroom is with them? But the days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for the patch pulls away from the garment and the tear is made worse.
Nor do people pour new wine into old wineskins. If they do, the skins burst, the wine spills, and the skins are ruined. No, they pour new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved."
While he was saying this, a ruler came and knelt before him, saying, "My daughter has just died. But come and lay your hand on her, and she will live."

versions.text: While he was saying this, a synagogue leader came and knelt before him, saying, "My daughter has just died. But come and lay your hand on her, and she will live."
versions.explanation: Matthew's text says simply ἄρχων ('a ruler'); the identification as a synagogue leader comes from the parallel accounts and is an interpretive addition here. If the fuller identification is desired, it is better placed in a footnote.

text: So Jesus got up and followed him, and so did his disciples.

versions.text: So Jesus got up and went with him, and his disciples followed.
versions.explanation: The Greek says Jesus followed the man (ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ), with the disciples doing the same; the current rendering reverses the picture by having the disciples follow Jesus rather than both following the ruler.

text: Just then a woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the edge of his cloak,
for she said to herself, "If I only touch his cloak, I will be healed."
Jesus turned and saw her, and he said, "Take heart, daughter; your faith has healed you." And from that moment the woman was well.
When Jesus came to the leader's house and saw the flute players and the crowd making a commotion,
he said, "Leave. The girl is not dead but asleep." And they laughed at him.
But when the crowd had been put outside, he went in, took her by the hand, and the girl got up.
And the news of this spread through that whole region.
As Jesus went on from there, two blind men followed him, shouting, "Have mercy on us, Son of David!"
When he had gone into the house, the blind men came to him, and Jesus asked them, "Do you believe that I am able to do this?" "Yes, Lord," they said.
Then he touched their eyes and said, "According to your faith let it be done for you."
And their eyes were opened. Then Jesus warned them sternly, "See that no one knows about this."

versions.text: And their eyes were opened. Jesus warned them sternly, "See that no one hears about this."
versions.explanation: γινωσκέτω means 'let no one know'; 'hears about' shifts the sense slightly and weakens the contrast with verse 31, where they spread the report.

versions.text: Jesus warned them sternly, "See that no one knows about this."
versions.explanation: The first clause of the verse, καὶ ἠνεῴχθησαν αὐτῶν οἱ ὀφθαλμοί ("and their eyes were opened"), has been dropped. This is the actual report of the healing and must be restored; without it the miracle itself is missing from the narrative. The corrected wording keeps the earlier revision's improvement of "knows about this" for γινωσκέτω.

text: But they went out and spread the news about him through that whole region.
As they were leaving, a man who was mute and possessed by a demon was brought to him.
And when the demon had been driven out, the man spoke. The crowds were amazed and said, "Nothing like this has ever been seen in Israel."
But the Pharisees said, "It is by the ruler of demons that he drives out demons."
Jesus went throughout all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness.
When he saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd.
Then he said to his disciples, "The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
So pray earnestly to the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest."

versions.text: So ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest."
versions.explanation: δεήθητε denotes earnest petition or prayer, not a simple request; 'pray' better conveys the force and preserves the prayer context of the saying.
